items.item: The form is split into titled sections (personal, job and contract, bank and tax, emergency contact, documents) in a single column, with a visible label above every field and no placeholder-only labels
items.evidence: Five <section> blocks with <h2> headings: 'Personal details', 'Job and contract', 'Bank and tax information', 'Emergency contact', 'Documents'. Every input has a <label class="block font-medium"> above it (e.g. <label for="firstName">First name *</label>); placeholders like placeholder="Minh" duplicate the label text rather than replacing it. Layout is a single max-w-3xl column (first/last name and city/postal are paired rows within that column, not separate columns).

items.item: Required fields are marked consistently, and optional fields are labelled as optional or left unmarked by a stated convention
items.evidence:
'* Required' legend at top (

* Required

), and every required field label includes '*' (e.g. firstName, email, department). Optional fields (preferredName, gender, city, postalCode, contractEndDate, workLocation, socialInsurance, dependents, emergencyAddress) carry no asterisk, consistent with the stated convention. Document rows go further with explicit 'Required'/'Optional' badges.

items.item: Field widths match their content: dates, postal codes and tax codes are narrow; inputs use the right types (email, tel, date)
items.evidence: dob/startDate/contractEndDate use class 'w-40' (narrow date fields), postalCode uses 'w-28'; taxCode/nationalId/socialInsurance use 'w-56' vs free-text fields using 'max-w-xl'. Types: type="email" on #email, type="tel" on #phone/#emergencyPhone, type="date" on #dob/#startDate/#contractEndDate.

items.item: An option to save the form as a draft is offered, and saving a draft does not demand every required field
items.evidence: #draft-btn 'Save draft' sets draftMode=true before calling submitForm(true); validateField() returns msg='' when draftMode is true and validateDocuments() skips the missing-required-docs check when draftMode is true, so draft save bypasses required-field/document validation.

items.item: Save and Cancel stay reachable while scrolling (a sticky bar or equivalent), Save is a verb label and is not disabled before submitting
items.evidence: <div class="sticky bottom-0 ... border-t border-border bg-card"> contains #cancel-btn, #draft-btn, and #save-btn labelled 'Save employee' with no disabled attribute present in markup; button only gets .disabled=true transiently inside submitForm()'s setTimeout simulation.

items.item: Fields validate on blur and on submit; with several errors a summary at the top links to each field and focus moves to the first invalid field
items.evidence: el.addEventListener('blur', () => { touched.add(name); validateField(name); }) validates per field on blur. submitForm() calls renderErrorSummary(), which (for items.length >= 3) renders '<ul>' with anchor links (href="#name", class="jump-link") that focus+scroll the target field on click, and separately focuses/scrolls the first invalid field (el.focus()) on submit.

items.item: Leaving the page with unsaved input triggers a warning
items.evidence: window.addEventListener('beforeunload', (e) => { if (!isDirty) return; e.preventDefault(); e.returnValue = ''; }) plus a custom #leave-dialog ('You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?') shown when Cancel is clicked while isDirty.

items.item: The document upload states accepted file types and the size limit, lists chosen files with a remove button, and is keyboard operable
items.evidence: Text: 'Accepted formats: PDF, JPG, PNG — up to 10 MB each.' Uploaded rows show fileName + size with a native <button class="doc-remove" aria-label="Remove {label}">Remove</button>; all upload/remove/preview controls are real <button> elements, so they are reachable and activatable via keyboard by default.

items.item: Success is confirmed with a message that names the employee and is announced to assistive technology
items.evidence: On submit, showToast('Employee Minh Nguyễn saved') names the employee, but the toast element is '<div id="toast" class="hidden fixed bottom-20 right-6 z-50 ...">' with no role="status"/role="alert"/aria-live attribute, so screen readers are not notified when it becomes visible. (Only #unsaved-indicator and #error-summary-wrap carry role="status"; #root-banner carries role="alert" but is never populated on success.)

notes: Automated audit score was 100/100 with no violations, but the success toast's missing aria-live/role causes the final checklist item to fail. No template tells (gradients, glass, uppercase tracked labels, emoji icons, rainbow status, promo cards, decorative charts, oversized radii, navy/indigo sidebar) were observed — the screen is a plain, flat single-column form with a neutral header bar.
